structured.approach: BE-03 asks me to confirm that the database changes the Backend tasks need are done. I read feat.tasks and feat.design to find any storage need for TSK-05 and TSK-06. I then checked ap_aging against the tool view and read src/ap_aging/aging.py and CLAUDE.md for its imports and stack. The design puts storage, database and schema migration outside its boundary, and the tool view says ap_aging has no database. So there are no required changes and the outcome holds. In the output I cite only what the cited sources state: I removed the file listing that no source supports, and I marked as agent judgement the inference about repeating the check if DES-01 reopens. I kept the tool-results block that the spine records at the end of the file.

claims.text: The design places storage, database and schema migration outside its boundary; the new data is one record key paid_date, one reject reason 'paid_date', and in-memory delay history, risk map, overdue rows and CT-1 JSON.
DD-1: no new repository, service, runtime, library or storage; only the Python 3.9 standard library and Node.js 22 CommonJS are used.

Every new function is pure and in-memory with no I/O, no network and no mutation of inputs (NF-10); a storage or network call from the libraries is a trigger that would reopen DES-01, and this design triggers none.
TSK-05 and TSK-06 change src/ap_aging/aging.py and src/ap_aging/__init__.py; TSK-05 depends on nothing in code and TSK-06 depends on TSK-05; TSK-06 adds no transport layer.
ap_aging has no database; no migrations exist or are required.
aging.py imports only date from datetime, Decimal from decimal, and Dict and Iterable from typing; aging_buckets loops over an iterable of invoice dicts and returns totals per bucket.
paid_date is a key of the in-memory invoice record (DC-1) built by transform.to_model in ap_pipeline under TSK-01; in ap_aging, extra keys such as paid_date are ignored.

structured.summary: This feature needs no database changes for the Backend lane (TSK-05, TSK-06 in ap_aging), and none are outstanding. feat.design keeps storage, schema and migrations out of scope (A1, DD-1, NF-10), and the tool view confirms ap_aging has no database and needs no migrations. So the step outcome holds because there are no required changes, and the Backend tasks can go ahead with no dependency on database administrators or infrastructure. The output task.db_changes now cites only statements its sources support, and the file listing that no source supported is removed. There are no blocking questions.
